theme: 3 terms on the view controller lifecycle: the object that runs one screen, the setup method that runs once, and the method that runs every time the screen shows

terms.definition: An object that manages one screen of an app: its views and what happens when the user taps them.
terms.example: Each tab has its own View Controller, so keep them small.

terms.definition: The method UIKit calls once, after a screen's view has been loaded into memory.
terms.example: Add the subviews in viewDidLoad, they only need to be created once.

terms.definition: The method UIKit calls every time a screen's view is about to appear.
terms.example: Reload the list in viewWillAppear, so it's fresh when the user comes back.

quizzes.question: In this code, which method should hold this line so it runs on every visit?
quizzes.code:
// refresh on every visit
nameLabel.text = user.name

quizzes.question: What do you call the object that manages one screen and its views?
Which method runs only once, right after the view is loaded into memory?

video.description:
Learn to explain the view controller lifecycle in UIKit: View Controller, viewDidLoad & viewWillAppear, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
View Controller - An object that manages one screen of an app: its views and what happens when the user taps them.
viewDidLoad - The method UIKit calls once, after a screen's view has been loaded into memory.
viewWillAppear - The method UIKit calls every time a screen's view is about to appear.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: UIKit View Controller, viewDidLoad & viewWillAppear | Day 82
landscape.description:
Explain View Controller, viewDidLoad & viewWillAppear in UIKit by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
뷰 컨트롤러, viewDidLoad, viewWillAppear 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

View Controller - An object that manages one screen of an app: its views and what happens when the user taps them.
한국어: 뷰 컨트롤러: 앱의 화면 하나를 맡아 그 화면의 뷰와 사용자가 탭했을 때의 동작을 관리하는 객체

viewDidLoad - The method UIKit calls once, after a screen's view has been loaded into memory.
한국어: viewDidLoad: 화면의 뷰가 메모리에 올라온 뒤 UIKit이 한 번 호출하는 메서드

viewWillAppear - The method UIKit calls every time a screen's view is about to appear.
한국어: viewWillAppear: 화면의 뷰가 나타나기 직전마다 UIKit이 호출하는 메서드

landscape.hook: You went back, but the screen shows old data. Can you explain why in English?

dialogue.title: Why is the old name back?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I changed my name, but the profile still shows the old one.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: In viewDidLoad, right after the `super` call.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That runs only once, when the View Controller first loads its view.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: But I went back to the profile. Doesn't it load again?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No, going back reuses the same View Controller, still in memory.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So where should the label update go?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Move it to viewWillAppear. It runs every time the view is about to show.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then should I keep anything in viewDidLoad?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, one time setup, like adding subviews. Keep viewDidLoad for that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. viewDidLoad builds the screen once, viewWillAppear refreshes `nameLabel` each visit.
One screen, one View Controller, keep it small.
